sources.publisher: New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (government)
sources.title: Driver’s Manual, Chapter 5: Intersections and Turns
sources.version: Live official driver manual; publication/update date not displayed in inspected passage
sources.locator: Right-of-Way: left-turn example immediately after the opposite-direction arrival bullet; wheels-straight and completion sentences
sources.excerpt: Keep your wheels straight to prevent being pushed into oncoming traffic if your vehicle is hit from behind.
sources.supports: Keep wheels straight while waiting to turn left across oncoming traffic; rear impact can push a pre-steered vehicle into the opposing path; turn when it can safely be completed.
sources.fallback_reason: Exact technique and rear-impact explanation not located through inspected TS/TRV searches. Direct government driver teaching is an appropriate fallback for this shared driving technique.
sources.scope_limits: Safety advice, not presented as a separately established Swedish statutory wheel-angle duty. Only wheel position and its risk explanation are used; New York right-of-way, junction-entry, signal and other legal instructions are not imported. Straight wheels reduce a risk, not guarantee protection.
sources.retrieval_method: Direct primary government web page retrieved and exact passage inspected

claims.required_statement_to_verify: Keep front wheels straight while waiting to turn left across oncoming traffic; explain the rear-impact risk.

source_searches.finding: No exact front-wheel waiting position/rear-impact passage located; related rules and test material did not establish this technique.
Infrastructure/left-turn crash-risk material found, but not exact wheel-position teaching. No claim that the technique is absent from every agency publication.
No exact directly published technique located.
